newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: US/French consortium wins Venezuela oil contract.
newsitem.headline: US/French consortium wins Venezuela oil contract.

text.p: A consortium comprising U.S. engineers Parsons, Halliburton subsidiary Brown and Root, and France's Technip has won a $1.056 billion contract to build a heavy crude processing unit in Venezuela, a Venezuelan official said on Thursday.
Carlos Jorda, president of the Petrozuata joint venture between Venezuelan state oil subsidiary Maraven and Conoco, said the contract should be signed on June 30.
The unit will convert 120,000 barrel per day of extra-heavy crude from Venezuela's Orinoco Belt into lighter grades for use in traditional refineries.
Jorda said plant construction was due to start in July or August, and start-up is scheduled for mid-2000.
The whole project was worth $2.464 billion, of which $690 million was start-up costs, $216 million was pipeline costs and $498 million was production costs, he added.
Petrozuata is hoping to start drilling in the Orinoco Belt in August, with an initial production of 30,000 bpd due in September 1998.
